title: Ywimpled
html_source:
The y- prefix is from Old/Middle English and is a way of signifying the past participle. Examples from Canterbury Tales include ybore (carried) and yfalle (fallen). It is cognate with the German prefix ge- (e.g., tragen= “to carry”; getragen = “carried”).

A wimple is a nun’s hood which covers the head and hair. I’m not sure what to make of the double markers for past tense here.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: According to Miriam-Webster, in Scotland, “wimple” could mean “curve” or “bend”. So, perhaps Joyce meant that Bloom was walking with his head down?
